newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: First National says first half lending up 88 pct.
newsitem.headline: First National says first half lending up 88 pct.

text.p: Ireland's First National Building Society (FNBS) said on Monday that it advanced 240 million Irish pounds in new loans in the first half of 1996, up 88 percent from 128 million in the same period last year.
In Britain, Mortgage Trust advanced 57 million stg in new loans after undertaking no new lending in the period from 1992 to July 1995, FNBS said in a statement.
But profits at Mortgage Trust were lower than in the same period last year, mainly due to pressure on net interest margins created by extensive discount pricing prevalent in the UK mortgage market.
Managing director John Smyth said that the UK economy continued to improve with clear indications of a significant pick-up in retail house prices and also in business and consumer confidence.
"The outlook for our business there is positive. I anticipate good profit growth as Mortgage Trust is now focused on specific, profitable product niches."

Smyth said the continuing reduction in the negative equity burden in the UK and the curtailment of the aggressive price discounting strategies seen recently underlined the potential for growth in the UK market.
FNBS said it expected Irish interest rates to remain at current levels with any upward movement likely to be small.

"The current low inflation, low interest rate environment is expected to continue. We anticipate sustained buoyancy in the mortgage market, particularly in retail housing with growth in house prices to the year-end likely to exceed 10 percent with stabilisation following in 1997," Smyth said.

He said that both consumer and business confidence remained high and the outlook for its core lending market remained positive although the building society expected intense competition in the retail savings market in Ireland.
Share and deposit balances rose by 55 million Irish pounds in the first half.
"Our priorities will be to continue to develop diversified sources of funding and to boost share balances," Smyth said.
Overall First National announced an 11 percent increase in half-year pre-tax profits to 9.71 million punts.

"These very satisfactory results reflect continuing strong performance across the core business areas. Lending activity in both Ireland and the UK has been exceptionally strong, reflecting the competitiveness of the group's product range," Smyth said.
FNBS estimated that its market share grew by two percent in the first half.

"The group's concentration in the short to medium term will be on consolidation and integration of its business with a specific focus both on cost containment and income growth," the building society said.
